chunks: 5140 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
A man came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and said: “My mother does not resist the hand of one who touches her.”
He said: “I have already done that.”
He said: “Then prevent anyone from entering upon her.”
He said: “I have already done that.”
He said: “Then restrain her, for you do not honor her with anything better than preventing her from violating the prohibitions of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.”

key_terms.فَامْنَعْ مَنْ يَدْخُلُ عَلَيْهَا: Prevent others from entering upon her
key_terms.لَا تَبَرُّهَا: You do not truly show dutiful goodness to her
key_terms.لَا تَدْفَعُ يَدَ لَامِسٍ: She does not resist illicit touching
key_terms.مَحَارِمِ اللَّهِ: The prohibitions and sacred limits set by Allah

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith define dutifulness to a mother when she persists in violating Allah’s prohibitions?
ai.summary: This hadith relates a legal-ethical ruling about preventing persistent immoral conduct, even when the person involved is one’s mother. It presents restraining her from falling into the prohibitions of Allah as a true form of dutifulness and care, rather than neglect or disrespect.
